summary: Muhamad Saputra is a doctoral student at the Australian National University, attested in 2026 studying under supervisor Assa Doron.

Archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar Muhammad Ashraf Khan served as Deputy Director of the Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums in Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Hanazono University (~1922–1925) and under Seisetsu Seki (~1929–1945). He was president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), abbot of Shofuku-ji (~1949–1988), and head of The Institute for Zen Studies (1964).

Buddhist studies scholar Mun-keat Choong studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute (1982), Komazawa University (~1986–1990), and the University of Queensland (~1991–1998 for MA and PhD), where he was supervised by Roderick S. Bucknell.

Munenobu Sakurai (born 1961) completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1986–1991) in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was an associate professor at Iwate University (~1995–2004) before becoming a professor at Tohoku University (~2004).

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) studied Indology and computational studies at Kyoto University (~1969–1971) and Harvard (PhD, ~1974–1984). He held an associate professorship at Tokyo Institute of Technology (attested 1983) and taught at Kyoto University as associate professor (~1988–1990) and professor (~1990–2009).
Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1910–1913) and studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (~1909–1913).
Mungunchimeg Batmunkh earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010), working in religious studies and Buddhist studies.

Munis D. Faruqui (born 1967) works in Indology and history. He has served as professor and undergraduate advisor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2006) and as Director and Sarah Kailath Chair of India Studies at the Numata Center (~2015).

Murray B. Emeneau (1904–2005) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton and Edgar Howard Sturtevant. He taught at Yale (1926) and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley (1940–1971).

Musashi Tachikawa (born 1942), working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earned degrees from Nagoya University and Harvard. He held posts at Nagoya University (1970), National Museum of Ethnology (~1992–2005; emeritus ~2005), and Aichi Gakuin University (~2005–2012).

Historian and Indologist Muzaffar Alam (born 1947) was educated at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He taught at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1973–2001) and was appointed George V. Bobrinskoy Professor at the University of Chicago (~2001).

Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at University College Dublin. He taught at Trinity College Dublin (1928–1930), University College Dublin (1930–1937), University of Wisconsin-Madison (1937), and directed the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (1960–1968).
Myokyo-ni (1921–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Graz and trained under Walter Nowick (~1960–1966) and Soko Morinaga (1984).

Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Madras Christian College (~1890–1895). He served as librarian at Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1891) and as professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College and the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas (1916–1999) earned degrees from Mysore, Mumbai, and Oxford. An Indologist, he taught at Oxford (~1948–1951), Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1951–1959), University of Delhi (1959), and chaired the Institute for Social and Economic Change (1972–1979).
Mónika Kiss is a doctoral student in Japanese studies and Buddhist studies at Eötvös Loránd University. She has studied under Masanori Yamaji (attested 2016), Robert F. Rhodes, and Nozomu Saito.

N. A. Jayawickrama (born 1920) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as professor at the University of Ceylon (~1958–1972) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.
N. Aiyaswami Sastri was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who served as a professor at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).
N. D. Mironov (1880–1936) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1901–1903) and under Hermann Jacobi and Heinrich Hübschmann (~1902–1904).
